item.title: Bilateral Agreements III: the Council of States opens the debate
item.description: The Council of States approved taking up the Switzerland-EU stabilization package for consideration by 29 votes to 15.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 29 votes to 15 in favour of entering into consideration - The package: 94 EU acts, 18 agreements and two declarations - Referendum: vote expected tomorrow - Debate in the chamber: over five hours
## Key facts - Subject → Swiss-EU stabilization package, Bilaterals III - Vote → 29 in favour and 15 against - Composition → 94 EU legal acts, 18 agreements and protocols, two joint declarations - Topics → referendum, state aid, wages, immigration, EU law, education and research - Discussion → presumably until Wednesday evening
## The vote in the Council of States
With 29 votes against 15, the Council of States entered into consideration today of the Swiss-EU stabilization package, Bilaterals III. The decision opens the detailed examination of a project made up of 94 EU legal acts, 18 agreements and protocols, and two joint declarations.
### An examination still open
The outcome came as no surprise: the camps had already formed. The UDC declared itself opposed to the entire package. The other parties, with some exceptions in the Centro and the PLR, together with the social partners and business associations, support the bilateral route in principle, but are demanding conditions.
The discussion of the details will presumably continue until Wednesday evening. The controversial points include the referendum, state aid, wage protection, immigration provisions, the dynamic adoption of EU law, and education and research. The examination of state aid began today and will continue tomorrow.
The debate on entering into consideration lasted over five hours and involved more than half of the members of the chamber. Federal Councillors Ignazio Cassis, Guy Parmelin and Beat Jans subsequently took the floor, respectively for foreign affairs, the economy, education and research, and justice and police.
On behalf of the Foreign Policy Committee, Carlo Sommaruga argued that a no could risk prolonging the erosion of the current agreements and, ultimately, of the foundation of Swiss prosperity. Fabio Regazzi, who also spoke for the Swiss Union of Arts and Crafts, which he chairs, urged that the door not be closed. He described the agreement as important for businesses and the free movement of persons, while acknowledging that wage protection, including protection against the dismissal of trade unionists, contains elements not welcomed by USAM. His final vote will also depend on how this is handled.
The discussion also touched on the referendum. Petra Gössi and Regazzi supported the double majority, meaning the people and the cantons, referring to the scope of the agreements and cantonal sovereignty. The vote on this point is expected tomorrow. ## The practical significance of the comparison
The source presents Bilaterals III as a decision with two levels. The first concerns the stability of relations with the largest economic partner. The second concerns the rules that, according to supporters and opponents, would define the future relationship between Switzerland and the EU. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the discussion therefore extends to businesses, mobility, wages, immigration, education and research.
The parliamentary procedure does not yet amount to an operational change. Entering into consideration opens the debate on the package; the effects depend on the details that the Chamber is examining. This distinction prevents political positions from being turned into obligations that are already valid.
### Four aspects to keep separate
| Aspect | Element reported by the source | Practical interpretation | |---|---|---| | Businesses and exports | Regazzi considers the agreement important for companies; Bischof and Würth refer to the cantons dependent on exports to the EU | The stability of economic relations is the point of reference for the productive fabric cited in the debate | | Movement of people | Free movement is described as important; the discussion also concerns EU directives on citizenship | The issue concerns the possibility of working and living in the European area mentioned by Moser | | Wages and work | USAM does not approve of certain aspects of wage protection, including protection against the dismissal of trade unionists | Wage protection remains a criterion for Regazzi's final vote | | Referendums and cantons | Optional and mandatory referendums are being compared, with a majority of the people or of the people and the cantons | The form of the vote is linked to legal certainty and cantonal sovereignty, according to supporters |
The reference to Brexit adds a concrete comparison to the debate. Tiana Angelina Moser argued that the status quo was not practicable and recalled that the United Kingdom, after losing access to the EU internal market, had harmed small and medium-sized enterprises. The source presents this as an argument in favor of bilateral continuity, not as an automatic prediction for Switzerland.
Opponents, on the other hand, view the dynamic adoption of Brussels law and case law as a problem for sovereignty. Marco Chiesa spoke about the role of the Court of Justice of the EU and possible compensatory measures; Ignazio Cassis challenged in the chamber the assertion that the Court would have the final say. Those consulting annunci di lavoro can therefore add the professional dimension to their reading of the rules still under discussion, without confusing the debate with a decision that is already applicable.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the next steps
The timetable indicated by the session allows for concrete monitoring, without anticipating the final outcome. The first rule is to distinguish what has already been voted on from what remains to be decided: the Council of States has voted to enter into the matter, while the details and the wording of the referendum are still under consideration.
### An operational checklist
1. Mark the immediate steps. The examination of state aid, which began today, will continue tomorrow. The vote on the nature of the referendum is scheduled for the same day. The discussion of the package may presumably continue until Wednesday evening.
2. Read the referendum using the exact wording. An optional referendum means, within the framework described in the chamber, a majority of the people. A mandatory referendum means a majority of the people and the cantons. Do not confuse the procedural choice with approval or rejection of the entire package.
3. Divide the news by dossier. Keep state aid, wage protection, immigration, free movement, dynamic adoption of EU law, education and research separate. These are the points indicated in the source; a statement on one of them does not automatically resolve the others.
4. Attribute each prediction to the person who formulated it. Supporters speak of stabilizing relations and the risk of erosion of the current agreements in the event of a no vote. Opponents speak of sovereignty, Brussels case law and possible compensatory measures. The report also states that Ignazio Cassis contested in the chamber the assertion that the EU Court of Justice has the final say. Separating these positions helps to follow the vote without treating a hypothesis as an established fact.
5. Connect the dossier to your situation only after clarifying the point concerned. A company can start with the economic relations with the EU area evoked in the debate; those considering a career change can consult the aziende che assumono, keeping the information tool distinct from the political outcome.
For a personal reference on income while the Council of States examines the package, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Bilateral Agreements III: Council of States enters into deliberations
item.description: The proposal to consider the bill was approved by 29 votes to 15. A new authority for state aid is planned, along with an extension of the hotel VAT rate to 3,8%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Bilaterals III: entry into the matter with 29 votes against 15 - State aid authority: 41 against 1, separate from COMCO - Hotel VAT: 3.8% rate until 2031
## Key facts - Vote on Bilaterals III → 29 against 15 in the Council of States - Supervisory authority → 41 against 1, independent from COMCO - Transitional period → five years from the entry into force of the agreements - Hotel rate → 3.8% until 2031 - Standard rate → 8.1% - Current deadline → end of 2027 - National Council vote → 101 against 86 and 7 abstentions
## The double parliamentary passage On September 28, 2026, the Council of States placed the future of relations between Switzerland and the EU at the center of parliamentary work. After an entry-into-the-matter debate that began at 2:38 PM, the chamber entered into the matter at 8:41 PM regarding the Switzerland-EU stabilization package, with 29 votes against 15. The detailed examination continued on state aid, and discussions were adjourned until Tuesday.
The vote showed a clear division. Against the entry into the matter were the seven representatives of the SVP and four Swiss-German exponents leading the Center and FDP. In favor were the SP, Greens, and Green Liberals, along with the remaining members of the Center and the FDP.
On behalf of the foreign policy committee, Carlo Sommaruga (SP/GE) recalled the deep ties with the European Union, Switzerland's primary trading partner. He defended a package intended to revitalize and strengthen existing bilateral agreements, warning that a 'no' would risk eroding current understandings. Marco Chiesa, representing the minority opposed to entering the merits, replied that the core issue is the resolution of disputes and that the agreements do not stabilize bilateral relations.
### Control over public aid The Council of States approved, with 41 votes against 1, the creation of a supervisory authority for state aid, separate from COMCO. The logic cited in the dossier is that of EU controls on aid granted by its members to avoid competition distortions in the internal market. Switzerland must create its own authority within a transitional period of five years from the entry into force of the agreements. Its opinion will be non-binding; if not respected, the authority will bring the case before a Swiss court.
In land transport, electricity, and air transport, the Confederation, Cantons, and Municipalities must notify every new public aid when it exceeds a certain threshold and is not subject to an exemption. Exceptions are provided, particularly for public transport operating solely within Switzerland.
### The hotel rate In the National Council, after the question hour, the plenum examined the divergences regarding the special rate for hotel services. With 101 votes against 86 and 7 abstentions, it decided to extend the reduced rate of 3.8% until 2031. The measure has been in effect since 1996 and has been extended six times. The dossier now returns to the Council of States. ## What changes in practical terms The vote on the agreements and the decision on VAT do not produce the same kind of consequence. The former opens a phase of parliamentary examination and introduces future oversight of public aid; the latter defines, for now in the National Council, a time horizon for the hotel rate. For those who live or work in Switzerland, distinguishing the two levels avoids reading as definitive what remains in the passage between the Chambers.
### A new filter for public aid The most operational point concerns the Confederation, Cantons and Municipalities. The notification is not described as general: the source links it to new aid in land transport, electricity and air transport, when it exceeds a certain threshold and does not benefit from an exemption. In terms of administrative work, each entity will therefore have to consider three elements together: sector, the new nature of the aid, and the applicability of a threshold or exemption. These are the conditions that, in the description of the package, trigger the notification.
If an entity prepares new aid in one of the sectors indicated, the procedure provided for by the package requires notification when the conditions are met. The authority's opinion is not binding, but failure to comply may bring the case before a Swiss court. The authority will be separate from COMCO: the oversight provided for by the package will therefore have a separate institutional reference. For public transport operators that operate solely in Switzerland, the source indicates exceptions.
### Three horizons for the hotel sector For the reduced rate, the compromise of the National Council should be read together with the alternatives that have already emerged. The source compares three outcomes:
| Parliamentary hypothesis | Rate or duration indicated | |---|---| | No entry into the matter at first reading | switch to the standard rate of 8,1% | | Decision of the National Council | extension of the reduced rate of 3,8% until 2031 | | Bill of the Federal Council and the Council of States | extension until 2035 |
The comparison does not indicate three simultaneous rates. It describes the path of the dossier: the extension to 2031 is the choice of the National Council, while the text returns to the Council of States. For a hotel business, the difference between the end-of-2027 deadline, the 2031 horizon and the 2035 proposal concerns the duration of the measure to be considered in planning, but the source does not yet close the passage between the Chambers.
To connect the topic to a personal budget without confusing VAT and taxes, one can use calcolatore stipendio e imposte. For the broader framework of costo della vita in Svizzera, the comparison should be kept separate from the parliamentary outcomes described here.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## The checklist for following the dossier The news report already provides a useful sequence for monitoring the next steps. The key is not to put Bilaterals III, state aid and hotel VAT on the same timetable: they have different votes, conditions and timelines.
### If following a public aid measure 1. Determine whether the aid is new and whether it falls under land transport, electricity or air transport. These are the three sectors indicated by the source. 2. Verify the two operational conditions: exceeding a certain threshold and the absence of an exemption. The source provides for notification when both apply. 3. If the conditions are met, the Confederation, the Cantons and the Municipalities must notify the measure to the new supervisory authority. The transitional period for establishing the authority is five years from the entry into force of the agreements. 4. Consider the outcome of the opinion: it is not binding, but if it is not followed, the authority brings the case before a Swiss court. Exceptions are provided for public transport services operating only in Switzerland.
### If following the hotel VAT rate To check the dates, the first reference point is the end of 2027, when the special rate expires according to the source. The second is 2031, the end of the extension chosen by the National Council; the third is 2035, indicated by the Federal Council's draft and the Council of States and supported by the minority. The ordinary rate of 8,1% should be kept as a scenario linked to not entering into the matter, while 3,8% is the scenario of the National Council's decision. The next step remains with the Council of States.
### If following the Switzerland-EU package To read the updates, it is useful to separate entry into the matter from detailed examination. The former was accepted; the latter continued on state aid and the discussions were updated to Tuesday. The report on the political phase indicates that the most intense debate will come with the examination of the individual agreements and accompanying measures. This distinction makes it possible to follow the dossier without confusing a procedural vote with approval of the entire package.

item.title: AI and work: different impact on women and men by 2030
item.description: By 2030, approximately 25% of activities performed by women and 28% of those performed by men could be automated; in the care, healthcare, and education sectors, the potential drops to 19%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- By 2030: approximately 25% of women's activities could be automated - For men, by 2030, 28% could be automated - Care, healthcare and education: 19% automation potential
## Key facts
- Research → Advance and McKinsey - Location → Zurich - Horizon → by 2030 - Women's activities → approximately 25% could be automated - Men's activities → 28% could be automated - Sectors → care, healthcare and education - Potential in these sectors → 19% - Interviewees → 26 human resources managers
By 2030, approximately 25% of the professional activities currently carried out by women could be automated, compared with 28% for men. This is the central finding of the new research conducted by Advance and McKinsey, which offers a less unfavorable outlook for women than the initial concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence on the world of work.
Automation could affect precisely some of the professional sectors in which women are most represented. The research points out, however, that many work in care, healthcare and education: fields in which human closeness, empathy and communication skills are difficult to replace.
### Where replacement is more difficult
The estimated automation potential in these sectors is 19%. This figure does not resolve the equation described by the research. According to the research, transformation requires understanding which tasks can be entrusted to AI and which depend on judgment, relationships and the ability to deal with unusual situations.
Nina Probst, co-author of the study, explained to 20 Minutes that approximately 25% of the human resources managers interviewed consider the growing importance of empathy, collaboration, judgment and interpersonal relationships an opportunity for women. She did, however, clarify that this advantage is not innate.
The research also describes a transformation of roles, not simply the elimination of the most exposed jobs. Customer service is given as an example: with fewer routine questions, agents could devote more time to complex cases and interaction with customers. For some of the 26 human resources managers interviewed, the work by Advance and McKinsey was a wake-up call: only a few had already explicitly considered gender differences in access to, use of or skills related to AI.
The point of the research therefore concerns preparation. Empathy and communication are gaining importance, but they are not enough on their own: one's position in the new world of work will also depend on the ability to use AI without giving up human judgment. The practical consequence for those working in Switzerland is not choosing between human and technical skills, but understanding how the weight of different tasks will change. The useful question becomes: which activities are repetitive, which require judgment, and which depend on interaction with other people? The research presents this distinction as a key interpretive lens.
### From routine work to complex cases
In customer service, the shift is clear. If AI answers routine questions, staff can devote more time to complex requests and customers. The role is not emptied out: the distribution of time changes and may become an opportunity to improve work.
| Work component | Evolution described by the research | |---|---| | Routine activities | Less room for repetitive responses | | Complex cases | More time devoted to handling and interaction | | Human skills and AI | Combination of knowledge and judgment |
For women working part-time in Switzerland, the same transformation has two sides. If AI performs routine tasks and makes knowledge more easily accessible, the relationship between hours worked and value produced may become less direct. But the work that remains may be more complex or require greater constant availability. The outcome will depend on companies' decisions about reorganizing work, not solely on the technological tool.
### Two career paths
The new professions identified by the research follow two directions. The first includes AI engineering, cybersecurity and big data, where women start from a lower presence in the talent pool. The second concerns transformation through AI, change management, governance, responsible use, ethics and training. These are roles that combine AI knowledge with human resources, communication, compliance and legal fields, areas in which women are already well represented.
Anyone considering a change can therefore read annunci di lavoro by looking not only for the name of the profession, but also for the type of skills required. The distinction helps separate a role focused on programming from one that integrates AI, relationships, judgment or organization. The research warns, however, that human skills alone are not sufficient: the decisive element remains the combination with practical knowledge of artificial intelligence.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. The research can be transformed into a concrete path without waiting for change to arrive in the form of a new role. The stated horizon is 2030; until then, the useful work consists of making visible which activities are carried out, which skills are used and where AI can enter without replacing judgment.
### Four operational steps
1. Map the activities. Separate routine activities from situations that require complex cases, customer relations, empathy or judgment. In customer service, the research describes precisely this shift: fewer repetitive responses, more interaction.
2. Learn about AI from a practical perspective. It is not necessary to equate competence with programming. What matters is understanding what the tool does well and where the result needs to be verified.
> «Being competent in artificial intelligence does not necessarily mean knowing how to program.»
Therefore, integrate the output with your own knowledge and judgment, avoiding blind trust in the results.
3. Cultivate the skills that remain central. Curiosity, the ability to learn and adapt, communication, emotional intelligence and interpersonal skills should be paired with critical thinking and problem-solving abilities. The question to keep open is whether what you are doing really makes sense.
4. Compare your profile with the two paths identified by the research. On the one hand, there are AI engineering, cybersecurity and big data; on the other, transformation through AI, change management, governance, responsible use, ethics and training. Skills in human resources, communication, compliance and the legal sector can become the basis for combining them with AI.
For those who manage people, the check to carry out is explicit: verify whether access to, use of and skills related to AI have also been examined from the perspective of gender differences. The research indicates that only a few of the 26 human resources managers interviewed had done so. For those who work part-time, it is instead worth asking how the company intends to distribute routine activities and what level of ongoing availability the remaining work will require: these are the two elements that the research identifies as possible opposing effects.
If the path leads to evaluating a new role, combine comparison with job postings with reading busta paga svizzera, so as to keep the content of the role separate from the current work situation. For the final step, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Vaud, 12% tax cut on income and wealth
item.description: Vaud approves a 12% reduction in cantonal income and substance taxes. There is talk of 272 million less from next January 1.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Vaud has voted in favor of a 12% tax reduction - 272 million less in revenue are expected - The Government has three months for the 2027 budget - The unions say they are ready to mobilize
## Key facts - Decision: yes to the initiative - Taxes: cantonal income and wealth taxes - Revenue: 272 million less - Deadline: next 1 January - State Council: two weeks for proposals - Assembly: 8 October
## The vote opens the budget dossier The Canton of Vaud has voted in favor of the initiative calling for a 12% reduction in cantonal taxes on the income and wealth of individuals. The figure indicated for the lower revenue is 272 million. The lost revenue is indicated as starting next 1 January, but the source does not yet indicate how the impact will be distributed among the different sectors.
For those living in the Canton, the vote therefore shifts the discussion from taxation to the sustainability of public services. The initiative’s proponents have promised that services will not be changed. Public services in Vaud are nevertheless on alert: the Government has three months to prepare the 2027 budget, and the question dominating the debate is where to make savings.
### The request to be consulted Jean-Luc Andrey, president of the Vaud association of medico-psycho-social institutions, recalled that during the 2025-2026 period, the institutions were presented with a fait accompli on the very day the budget was presented. He asked that the institutions be consulted, whatever decision affects them.
> “In 2025-2026, we were presented with a fait accompli on the very day the budget was presented. We do not want this to happen again: we are asking to be consulted, whatever decision is made regarding our institutions.”
The State Council has given itself two weeks to present its proposals to Parliament. In the meantime, the municipalities are watching the dossier because they are on the front line in managing services for citizens. Chantal Weidmann-Yenny, PLR president of the Association of Vaud Municipalities, identified as a risk the possibility that the municipalities would have to make up the revenue shortfall. She called for joint work with the Canton on infrastructure regulation and the issue of housing.
The unions have already announced possible mobilization if cuts are introduced. Catherine Friedli, SSP Vaud union secretary, said that there are already insufficient resources to guarantee the quality of public services and staff working conditions. The public service staff assembly is scheduled for 8 October, during the electoral period preceding the renewal of Parliament and Government scheduled for next February. ## The reduction is not the same as the entire tax To understand the effect on the household budget, it is necessary to separate the levels of the Swiss tax system. The system comprises direct federal tax, cantonal taxes and municipal taxes; the Cantons have their own law and multiplier, while municipalities apply a multiplier to the cantonal tax. The initiative approved in Vaud concerns the cantonal component of income and wealth tax for individuals. Thus, by its subject matter, it is not an intervention concerning direct federal tax or VAT.
The same distinction avoids confusing the vote with other items that affect personal finances. The reduction does not concern AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, which are social security, nor LAMal/KVG, which is compulsory health insurance with per-capita premiums. It is not a measure concerning the minimum wage. The cost of living in Switzerland may change the concrete weight of a tax decision for a family, but the source does not provide an individual calculation or a new overall rate. The 12% therefore does not correspond to 12% of the entire personal tax burden.
### Three scenarios to follow The first scenario is the one promised by the promoters: services remain unchanged even after the cut. In this case, practical verification comes through the 2027 budget and the Government's proposals. The source does not yet list the sectors concerned or indicate a savings plan.
The second scenario is the one feared by the municipalities. If the revenue shortfall were to fall on them, the discussion would shift to the local management of services, infrastructure and housing. This is a concern expressed by the Union of Vaud Municipalities, not a decision already taken.
The third scenario is the trade-union one. If the savings entailed cuts, SSP Vaud announces mobilization and puts service quality and working conditions at the center. The staff assembly thus becomes an event to monitor, alongside the renewal of Parliament and Government next February.
| Scenario | What the source indicates | What to verify | |---|---|---| | Promoters' promise | Services without changes | 2027 budget | | Municipalities' concern | Possible deficit coverage | Canton's proposals | | Trade-union position | Mobilization in the event of cuts | Service conditions |
To focus on the personal budget, it is advisable to compare the tax component with other expenses, without calling something related to premiums or pension provision a tax reduction. The costo della vita in Svizzera helps put this picture into perspective. The dichiarazione delle imposte remains the reference for one's own tax situation, but it does not replace the decisions that the Canton still has to present.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to follow the decision The source leaves two elements open for anyone who has to estimate the concrete effect: the measure has been approved, but the State Council still has to present its proposals and the Government has to prepare the 2027 budget. For now, therefore, the useful procedure is a sequence of checks on public decisions, not a simulation based solely on 12%.
### Four practical steps 1. Mark the next 1° gennaio as the reference date for the announced lower revenue. The source provides only the overall figure of 272 million less, not a personal amount. 2. Wait for the proposals of the State Council, which has given itself two weeks to submit them to Parliament. This is the first institutional step indicated after the vote. 3. Follow the 2027 budget over the three months assigned to the Government. The point to verify is whether and how public services will be affected, given that the proponents have promised not to change their provision. 4. For those who work in public service or use municipal services, observe the discussion between the Canton, municipalities and unions. The staff assembly is scheduled for 8 ottobre; the renewal of Parliament and Government is expected next febbraio.
### How to avoid hasty interpretations It is not enough to multiply a personal figure by 12%. The source does not specify the remaining rates, the methods of application, any municipal indications, or how the lower revenue will be absorbed into public accounts. For this reason, the check must be carried out on two levels: on the one hand, the effect on one's own cantonal taxation; on the other, the budget choices that may affect services.
For the individual part, one can organize one's situation in dichiarazione delle imposte, distinguishing the cantonal component from the other tax items. This step does not yet make it possible to know a definitive saving, because the source does not publish a calculation by income or assets.
Political communication will also have an operational role: the proponents' promises, the State Council's proposals, Parliament's decisions, and the unions' response are different steps. Confusing them leads to presenting as already decided what remains to be defined, particularly with regard to municipalities and services.
The reader can therefore update their overview when the budget documents arrive and compare the items without conflating taxes, social security and insurance premiums. To estimate the effect on the personal budget, use calcolatore stipendio e imposte.

item.title: UBS under pressure: 90% capital for foreign branches
item.description: Council of States calls for 90% capital for UBS's foreign subsidiaries. The bank contests the measure, rekindling speculation about a merger with Morgan Stanley and other institutions.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Council of States calls for 90% capital for foreign subsidiaries. - UBS challenges the capital measure. - Blick cites at least eight institutions, with Morgan Stanley among the names. - Relocating the headquarters could affect tax revenues.
## Key facts - Decision → 90% core capital for UBS's foreign subsidiaries - Institution → Council of States - UBS's reaction → political outcome described as not a compromise - Potential counterparts → at least eight globally active financial institutions - Name cited → Morgan Stanley - Analyst → Rudolf Minsch, chief economist at Economiesuisse - Second expert → Aymo Brunetti, professor at the University of Bern - Tax effect → tax revenues if the headquarters are relocated
### The decision and assumptions about the future
ZURICH - The battle over the new rules for UBS is entering a new phase following the Council of States' request: the large Swiss bank should support its foreign subsidiaries with core capital amounting to 90%. UBS challenges the measure.
> UBS described the political outcome as «not a compromise».
According to an investigation by Blick, the upper chamber's decision has reignited speculation about a possible merger. At least eight globally active financial institutions are said to have expressed openness to talks with UBS's management. Among the names cited is Morgan Stanley, a US institution.
The discussion stems from two distinct but related elements in the debate: the capital requirement for foreign operations and possible talks with other global groups. The source thus describes the merger as a possibility reignited by the political decision.
Rudolf Minsch, chief economist at Economiesuisse, argues that UBS would not give up its corporate banking business in Switzerland. Any downsizing, however, could create difficulties, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly with regard to larger financing needs. Companies could therefore be forced to seek financing elsewhere, including abroad.
Aymo Brunetti, a professor at the University of Bern, takes a more reassuring view. In his opinion, a possible merger or relocation of the headquarters would be unlikely to have immediate consequences for private and corporate clients. UBS would continue to have an interest in keeping its private and corporate banking activities in Switzerland because they are profitable. The most visible effects could concern tax revenues if the headquarters were relocated.
Brunetti also considers both a merger and a relocation of the headquarters unlikely at present. Swiss identity would remain important, especially in wealth management; becoming a US bank could make UBS less attractive to some international clients, particularly in Asia. The new capital requirement could ultimately make expansion in the United States more difficult, one of the reasons for UBS's strong opposition, according to the economist. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical point is not choosing a future partner for UBS, but distinguishing which activities would be affected in the different scenarios described by the experts. The source compares corporate lending, customer services and tax domicile: three connected but not equivalent areas.
### Four scenarios to keep separate
The first concerns corporate banking. If the bank were to scale back its operations in Switzerland, according to Rudolf Minsch, small and medium-sized enterprises would be the most exposed when seeking large amounts of financing. In this scenario, the issue is not presented as a general difficulty for every customer, but as the risk of having to seek credit elsewhere, including outside the country. For a company, the concrete question is therefore how dependent it is on UBS for its larger transactions.
The second scenario is a merger or relocation of the headquarters. Aymo Brunetti considers immediate consequences for private and corporate customers difficult, because UBS would have an interest in retaining private and corporate banking in Switzerland, which are profitable activities. This reduces the idea of an automatic effect on banking relationships, without eliminating the issue of the headquarters.
| Scenario | Effect indicated in the source | |---|---| | Scaling back | Possible difficulties for small and medium-sized enterprises, especially with larger financing | | Merger or relocation | Difficult immediate consequences for private and corporate customers | | Relocation of the headquarters | Possible effects on tax revenues | | Possible US bank | Potentially lower appeal for some customers in Asia | | New requirement | Possible expansion in the United States becoming more difficult |
For those who manage conti bancari in Svizzera, this distinction helps avoid confusing service continuity with broader economic consequences. The third and fourth scenarios in fact concern the taxation of the headquarters, the international appeal of Swiss identity and UBS's ability to expand in the United States. The source does not present them as a single outcome, but associates them with the different hypotheses. The decisive variable therefore remains the form that any change might take, not merely the fact that names of possible partners are circulating.

Società Navigazione del Lago di Lugano (SNL) has begun a reorganization following the decision by Canton Ticino to no longer commission the navigation service on the Locarno-Magadino route and not to cover any potential deficits. The company maintains that the decision by the Council of State will result in expected losses of between 350'000 and 400'000 francs.

According to SNL, the cantonal decision made cost containment necessary. The company says it has managed, «at least at this stage», to limit the consequences for staff: measures that are «less burdensome for staff» have been identified, and redundancies have been reduced to a minimum. The people involved were offered an «alternative contract». The possibility of signing it remains open even for those who had initially chosen not to accept it.
The assessment of the decision remains critical. SNL recalls that it took on the service on Lake Maggiore at the request of the Ticinese and federal authorities, providing public transport services over the years. In its view, the withdrawal of cantonal support unilaterally altered the economic conditions on which the service had been structured.
The matter thus affects the company's operations and the continuity of the service. The stated objective is to maintain an adequate level of service without excessively increasing ticket prices. SNL emphasizes that fares had been kept down because the services had been conceived as public transport and not as a simple commercial tourist offering.
> «We chose to do everything within our power to protect jobs and, at the same time, continue to guarantee a service to the region», says director Simone Bianchi.
In the coming weeks, SNL will continue to assess various operational and commercial scenarios. The statement thus leaves the way open both regarding staff and the service on Lake Maggiore. ### Before and after: where the economic risk shifts
The difference between the previous situation and the one described by SNL concerns how the navigation service is supported. ## The German decision reshapes Migros's exit
ZURICH - Migros will have to find new buyers for 24 Tegut supermarkets in Germany. The German antitrust office has authorized Edeka to take over 178 of the 202 stores initially planned. The 24 excluded stores remain outside the transaction for competition-related reasons.
The approved package also includes 41 Teo automated stores, the Herzberger bakery and a logistics center. The sale therefore does not concern only the traditional supermarket network: these elements are part of the scope Edeka may take over.
Other buyers will be sought for the remaining stores, a spokesperson for the Migros Zurich cooperative explained to the AWP news agency. Migros welcomed the green light and says that its exit from the German food retail market is proceeding according to plan.
### Why the transaction was reduced
The German antitrust authority had been examining the transactions since March. According to the authority, the acquisition originally envisaged would have significantly hindered competition in 34 regional markets in Hesse, Thuringia, northern Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg. In nine of these markets, Edeka would also have established or strengthened a dominant position.
The assessment takes place in a highly concentrated German retail market. In 2025, Edeka, Rewe, the Schwarz Group, owner of Lidl and Kaufland, and Aldi accounted for more than 90% of total sales. Edeka was the largest operator, with a share of approximately 30%.
Tegut has belonged to Migros Zurich since 2013 and employs approximately 7'400 people. The closure of the Fulda headquarters is planned for the end of March 2027. Operations that are not transferred to a buyer will be liquidated as part of reconciliation-of-interests agreements and social plans.

### New requirements for farms
BERN - The Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (USAV) has defined new biosecurity requirements for pig farms. The objective indicated by the office is to protect animals from African swine fever, ASF.
The new development concerns so-called ASF compliance. Pig farms that meet the requirements may benefit from facilitations in animal movements if an epidemic occurs. The communication does not limit the scope to professional facilities: the rules apply to all pig farms, from professional breeding and fattening operations to hobby operations.
The requirements were developed in collaboration with companies in the sector, USAV announced. The collaboration therefore concerns the definition of the conditions for ASF compliance, while the communication attributes the definition of the new requirements to the federal office.
### What level 1 includes
The measures required include, first and foremost, the systematic prevention of any contact between domestic pigs and wild boars. This is followed by clearly defined access controls and hygiene measures at the entrance to the stables.
Biosecurity also includes documentation. USAV specifies complete and up-to-date documentation, including the visitor register, treatment log and daily recording of deaths and abortions.
The requirements now published concern level 1, intended for periods of calm, such as the current one. If an epizootic outbreak were to occur, the level would move to level 2, with additional measures adopted. The communication thus distinguishes between the procedures envisaged during the ordinary phase and those that would come into force during a health emergency. ## What changes at the operational level
The distinction between level 1 and level 2 helps read the measure as a graduated system. At level 1, which applies during periods of calm, biosecurity is based on the requirements published by USAV. In the event of an epizootic disease outbreak, the system instead moves to level 2, which entails adopting additional measures. The source specifies the change in level, but does not list the supplementary measures.
For a farm, PSA compliance does not consist of a single check. It is a set of interconnected practices and records. The separation of domestic pigs and wild boar concerns contact prevention; access control concerns who enters; hygiene concerns entry into the barns; records make the activities and events indicated by USAV documentable.

## In brief - Parliament and the Cantons have resolved the last divergence - Preference for overhead lines at 220 kV, except in certain cases - Over 60% of extra‑high‑voltage lines will reach end‑of‑life - The dossier is ready for final votes
## Key facts - Where → Bern - What → Revision of the Electricity Installations Act - Objective → Accelerate grid expansion - Threshold → 220 kV for preference of overhead lines - Distribution network → nominal voltage above 36 kV - Extra‑high‑voltage lines reaching end‑of‑life → over 60% - Transformation stations → maximum 20 m² and 3 metres - Dossier status → ready for final votes
Today, in Bern, the two chambers of Parliament reached an agreement on the revision of the Electricity Installations Act. The Cantons aligned with the National Council, clearing the last divergence. The dossier, devoted to accelerating expansion and simplifying grid transformation, is therefore ready for final votes.
### A grid to be expanded and renewed
The revision aims to support the energy transition by reducing bureaucratic delays and favouring grid efficiency. The dossier gives a two‑fold reason: the grid must meet growing demand while also being renewed. Over 60% of extra‑high‑voltage lines will reach end‑of‑life, while electricity line projects proliferate and authorisations take several years.
One central point concerns overhead lines. When voltage is equal to or greater than 220 kilovolts, preference will be given to them, except in certain cases. In buildable zones, lines may instead be buried. Parliament reintroduced the principle that the Federal Council had removed from the draft after strongly negative feedback from the consultation.
On the current route or in its immediate vicinity, existing high‑voltage lines may be replaced without a sectoral planning procedure. Parliament extended the rule to extra‑high‑voltage lines along national highways and railway lines, and to distribution‑network lines with a nominal voltage above 36 kV.
If pylons need to be moved, legal distances from forests and watercourses may be disregarded. Outside buildable zones, existing lines may be replaced even beyond the limits for noise and non‑ionising radiation, provided exposure does not increase further. Inside buildable zones, suitable measures must be verified to reduce it.
Transformation stations may also be built more easily outside buildable zones. They need not be directly adjacent to that zone: the ground footprint may not exceed 20 m² and the maximum height will be 3 metres. It will also be possible to replace or modify stations lawfully constructed outside buildable zones, provided no overriding interest opposes it. ## What changes when reading a project
For those who live or work near an electrical infrastructure, the difference does not lie in a single rule, but in the type of intervention. The revision distinguishes the replacement of existing lines from the expansion of the network and distinguishes the building zone from the area outside it. This framework makes it possible to understand where the text reduces a procedural step and where, instead, it maintains checks related to exposure.
### Before assessing a route
The first question is whether it concerns an existing line on the current route or in the immediate vicinity. For these replacements, the sectoral plan procedure is not required in the cases indicated by the revision. Parliament has also extended the principle to ultra-high-voltage lines along national roads and railway lines and to the distribution network with a nominal voltage above 36 kV.
The second question concerns the location. In building zones, undergrounding remains possible for lines with a voltage of 220 kV or more. Outside the building zone, existing lines may also be replaced beyond the noise and non-ionizing radiation limit values, but only if exposure does not increase further. Within the building zone, the text requires appropriate measures to reduce it to be verified. These are differences to check in the project.
| Situation to be verified | Criterion provided for by the text | |---|---| | Existing line on the route or in the immediate vicinity | Replacement without a sectoral plan procedure | | Building zone | Undergrounding of 220 kV lines possible | | Outside the building zone | Replacement beyond the limit values if exposure does not increase | | Transformer station | Outside the building zone, even if not adjacent; maximum 20 m2 and 3 metres |
The third key is the balancing of interests. Except in certain cases, a secure and economical energy supply will prevail over territorial protection and planning. The Federal Council intended to grant this overriding interest to the transmission network; Parliament extended it to the distribution network above 1 kV. The reader must therefore keep two aspects distinct: on the one hand, the security and cost-effectiveness of supply, and on the other, the territorial and exposure conditions laid down for the various interventions.

A practical review can follow four steps. This is a way to apply the distinctions contained in the revision to the project's characteristics.
### Four checks
1. Classify the intervention. Check whether it concerns an existing line located on the current route or in the immediate vicinity, or a transformer substation. The simplification described by the source refers to the replacement of lines in the indicated cases and also allows stations legally built outside the building zone to be replaced or modified, when no overriding interest opposes this.

Within the building zone, appropriate measures to reduce exposure must instead be verified.
3. Check the network and voltage. These are different reference points and must be read separately.
4. Verify the physical elements. For a transformer substation outside the building zone, check the ground area, which may not exceed 20 m2, and the maximum height of 3 meters. ## In brief - Italian extra‑UE exports: +16.1% year‑on‑year - Switzerland: +57%, with gold bullions standing out - United States: +31.1%, with acceleration in pharmaceuticals - Istat: the detailed data will arrive later
## Key facts - Period → August - Area → extra‑UE countries - Overall growth → +16.1% year‑on‑year - Switzerland → +57% - United States → +31.1% - Leading goods → intermediate and capital goods - Switzerland → gold bullions - United States → pharmaceuticals
In August, Italian exports to extra‑UE countries recorded a strong year‑on‑year increase of +16.1%. The indication comes from the National Institute of Statistics, Istat, which in the press release highlights two destinations with marked increases: Switzerland, with +57%, and the United States, with +31.1%.
For Switzerland, the more specific reference is to gold bullions. The source does not yet present the full detail of the transactions: it states that the data will be published later. The available data therefore allows us to identify the category indicated by Istat, but not to establish quantities, absolute values or individual operators involved.
Istat attributes the growth of extra‑UE exports mainly to the rise in sales of intermediate and capital goods. The formulation refers to the general picture of Italian exports outside the European Union. The reference to gold bullions is instead linked in particular to the Swiss direction. For the United States, the press release signals an acceleration concerning pharmaceuticals.
### Three percentages, three perimeters
The reading must keep the three numbers separate. The 16.1% relates to the total of Italian exports to extra‑UE countries; the +57% refers to growth towards Switzerland; the +31.1% concerns growth towards the United States. These are three percentages with different scopes.
For those living in Switzerland, the national point of the news is the country’s role as a destination cited in the Italian data and the association with gold bullions. The press release does not describe effects on families, prices or Swiss incomes. Even the cost of living in Switzerland remains a different indicator: the Istat note talks about exports, not cost of living.
## The scope of the signal for Switzerland
The Italian data provides a precise signal about the direction of sales, but not a complete picture of the Swiss economy. The source links exports to Switzerland, in particular, to gold bars; however, it does not explain whether the growth depends on an increase in quantities, different unit values or a combination of elements. Without the detail announced by Istat, these hypotheses cannot be selected.
The same limitation applies to the national reading. The news does not indicate Swiss locations, operators, final recipients or the duration of the phenomenon. It does not attribute the growth to a political decision, a tax change, a customs rule or a change in prices. Including one of these elements would mean going beyond the press release.
### The correct comparison
It is instead possible to compare the overall non-EU scope with the two named destinations. The first measure describes the general trend; the other two isolate individual directions. The goods must also be kept distinct: intermediate and capital goods are the driver indicated for the whole, gold bars are the specific reference associated with Switzerland, and pharmaceuticals are the acceleration reported for the United States. This sequence cannot be turned into a complete ranking, because the text does not list all destinations or all categories.
For a Swiss reader, the practical consequence is a single, very concrete one: use the data to understand how the Swiss destination is described in the press release, not to estimate the impact on prices, incomes or consumption independently. Any currency comparison, when amounts become available, can be made with comparatore CHF/EUR, but the tool does not replace the Istat detail and does not convert a percentage into an absolute value.
This approach avoids two errors: reading the +57% as an already quantified sum of money, or presenting gold bars as the only export item to Switzerland. The source says that the category concerns those exports in particular, not that it accounts for the entire flow.

For those who want to follow the data from the Swiss side, the operational step is to keep scope, destination, and goods separate. The source already indicates that the detail will arrive later: this is the only explicit timing milestone, so it must not be replaced with an invented deadline.
1. Start with the period: note that the communication concerns August. Every comparison must maintain the same period and the same annual basis indicated by Istat.
2. Separate the destinations: read the Switzerland line without transferring to it the data referring to the United States. The former is associated with gold bars; the latter with pharmaceuticals. This avoids attributing the pharmaceutical acceleration to Switzerland.
3. Await the detailed data: until they are published, record only the data already communicated and the category indicated. Do not add quantities, amounts, companies, locations, or reasons not present in the note.

item.title: ORS takeover at asylum centers: guarantees requested
item.description: ORS’s takeover of the federal asylum centers is scheduled for January 1, 2027; AOZ employs 120 people in Ticino and, if Chiasso does not reopen, up to 40 positions are at risk.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 1 gennaio 2027: ORS takeover expected - AOZ Ticino employs 120 people at cantonal level - If Chiasso does not reopen, around 40 employees could be affected - Assembly organised by VPOD in Balerna
## Key facts - What → ORS taking over assistance at federal asylum centres - Decision → SEM - Expected date → 1 gennaio 2027 - AOZ employment → 120 people at cantonal level - Chiasso scenario → around 40 employees affected if the centre does not reopen - Assembly → venerdì 25 settembre, Balerna - Union → VPOD - Cantonal role → OCST and the Personnel Commission
On venerdì 25 settembre, AOZ Ticino staff gathered in Balerna for an assembly organised by the VPOD union. At the centre of the discussion is the failure to win the contract for providing assistance at federal asylum centres and the planned takeover by ORS, decided by SEM as of 1 gennaio 2027.
The concern relates to three interconnected areas: jobs, employment conditions and the quality of care provided to asylum seekers. AOZ employs 120 people at cantonal level. According to the statement, their experience has ensured operational continuity and expertise in providing assistance for years.
According to the assembly, the change of operator risks having a serious impact on employment. The termination of some employment relationships has already been envisaged. If the federal asylum centre in Chiasso does not reopen, around 40 employees could be affected.
### The issue of the collective labour agreement
A second element concerns AOZ's collective labour agreement, which is in force and based on the employment conditions of the City of Zurich. The assembly points to the lack of guarantees that it will be maintained, while ORS has not signed a CCL. The feared consequence is twofold: job losses and a deterioration in employment conditions.
This prospect is situated in a region already affected by employment difficulties and by other cutbacks linked to the Confederation. The statement cites the one involving FFS Cargo between Mendrisio and Chiasso.
The assembly calls on the Federal Council, SEM, AOZ and ORS to fulfil their respective social responsibilities. It demands an immediate dialogue with the social partners, complete information and concrete guarantees for employment and working conditions. It also challenges the approach that rules out recognising a transfer of business to ORS and the consequent transfer of employment relationships, without clear redeployment guarantees, especially in Ticino.
The statement recognises VPOD's national role and, at cantonal level, the role of OCST and the Personnel Commission in the collective representation and protection of employees. Those seeking an alternative job can consult annunci di lavoro. The practical issue for staff is not only who will manage the centers from 1 January 2027. The note separates at least three questions: whether the employment relationships will continue, under what conditions and with what effect on care provision. Placing them on the same level instead obscures the differences between a change of operator and a reduction in activity linked to Chiasso.
### A comparison on three levels
| Element | Situation described | Scenario indicated by the assembly | | --- | --- | --- | | Employment | AOZ employs 120 people in Ticino | some employment relationships could end; around 40 employees if Chiasso does not reopen | | Employment conditions | CCL AOZ in force, linked to the conditions of the City of Zurich | no guarantee of continuation; ORS has not signed a CCL | | Service | AOZ's experience associated with continuity and expertise | the change of operator risks affecting the quality of care provision |
This comparison clarifies why the assembly is asking for guarantees before the takeover and not merely information about the name of the new operator. The first scenario concerns the continuity of jobs; the second concerns the content of the work; the third concerns the asylum seekers assisted in the federal centers.
The territorial impact indicated in the source is specific: the possible failure to reopen Chiasso would compound the employment difficulties and the downsizing of FFS Cargo between Mendrisio and Chiasso. The figure of around 40 employees is linked, in the note, specifically to the possibility that Chiasso will not reopen.
According to the assembly, responsibility is shared between federal bodies and operators. For this reason, the request for discussions involves the Federal Council and SEM, but also AOZ and ORS. The trade union representation is twofold: VPOD as the national representative; OCST and the Staff Commission in the cantonal representation.
To better understand the elements that make up an employment condition, one can consult the guide to busta paga svizzera. The link does not replace the guarantees requested by the assembly, but it helps distinguish the employment relationship from the individual conditions.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. To turn the assembly’s requests into a verifiable process, the date to keep in mind is 1 January 2027, the scheduled date for ORS to take over, as decided by SEM. The requests set out in the note can be organized into five steps, all connected to employment and working conditions.
### The sequence of requests
1. Request an immediate discussion between the social partners, Federal Council, SEM, AOZ and ORS. This is the first commitment highlighted by the assembly in order to achieve the requested guarantees.
2. Obtain complete information about the takeover. The discussion must cover the mandate for assistance, continuity of positions, working conditions and the quality of care, issues indicated in the position statement.
3. Verify the retention of all existing positions. The main demand is the transfer of employment relationships from AOZ to ORS; if necessary, appropriate redeployments in the region are also requested, with the support of external experts.
4. Exclude demotions and ensure duties and conditions that are at least equivalent. The request concerns both the transfer of employment relationships and any redeployment solutions.
5. Keep the case of the federal asylum center in Chiasso separate. The failure to reopen it is indicated as the scenario in which approximately 40 employees could be affected; it is not the same as the operator’s takeover.
### The parties to involve
The representation indicated by the assembly is structured across several levels. VPOD is recognized as the national point of contact; at the cantonal level, OCST and the Personnel Commission have a role in representing and collectively protecting employees. AOZ and ORS are called upon to discuss the conditions, while the Federal Council and SEM are reminded of the social responsibilities linked to the decision.
The date indicated for the start is therefore 1 January 2027: the assembly’s demand concerns the guarantees to be defined before the takeover. Anyone who wants to supplement the assessment of the conditions with a review of their own income can use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Joseph Deiss: we want an active and evolutionary neutrality
item.description: Over seven out of ten voters rejected the initiative for stricter neutrality; Deiss, at La Matinale RTS, stresses the need for active and evolutionary neutrality.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - More than seven in ten voters reject the initiative - The text limited sanctions and cooperation with NATO - Joseph Deiss defends an active and evolving neutrality - The Council of States opens the debate on Bilaterals III
## Key facts - Outcome → rejection of the neutrality initiative - Subject → stricter definition of neutrality in the Constitution - Appearance → Joseph Deiss, Monday on RTS's La Matinale - Constitution → 1999 text - Debate → Bilateral III agreements with the European Union - Initiative cited → Bussola - Expected majority → double majority of the people and the Cantons
More than seven in ten voters rejected on Sunday the initiative that sought to enshrine a stricter definition of Swiss neutrality in the Constitution. The text would have limited the adoption of sanctions and military cooperation with alliances such as NATO.
### The vote and Deiss's reading
On Monday, a guest on RTS's La Matinale, Joseph Deiss reacted with irony to the breadth and uniformity of the result. The former federal councillor, who headed Foreign Affairs for four years, saw a political effect in Christoph Blocher's initiative: it would have united the country against the text and bridged the Röstigraben.
> This initiative by Christoph Blocher had one merit: uniting the country against it. The Röstigraben was bridged, and it achieved a score that could even be described as Soviet.
For Deiss, the vote offers two lessons. The population would have understood that Switzerland cannot guarantee its own security alone by distancing itself from its European neighbors. Moreover, it would be tired of the country's sometimes overly timid stance in the face of international crises, particularly in Ukraine and Gaza.
### An open-ended neutrality
The rejection maintains current policy, but Deiss does not consider it a blocking status quo. In his view, the result leaves the Federal Council, Parliament and citizens the possibility of shaping foreign policy.
The former minister recalled that the 1999 Constitution, in whose drafting he took part, does not precisely define neutrality. The choice, he explained, was deliberate: as in 1848, neutrality was to remain a tool of security and defense policy, not an end in itself.
The result confirms an evolving conception. Deiss speaks of an active and engaged neutrality, capable of evolving with international law and the institutions created after the Hague Conventions. His reasoning includes the Charter of the United Nations, the Geneva Conventions and the International Criminal Court, which, in his view, make it impossible to treat an aggressor and their victim in the same way.
Hence the call for the Federal Council to adopt a consistent line on violations of international law. Deiss invoked Switzerland's responsibility as depositary of the Geneva Conventions and warned that failing to condemn war crimes can make the country complicit. He also invoked the values of peace, solidarity and humanity that, in his view, his compatriots want to see defended by Switzerland. The result produces a precise institutional effect: the stricter definition proposed by the initiative does not enter the Constitution. The current policy is maintained and, according to Joseph Deiss's reading, the Federal Council, Parliament and the population retain room to shape foreign policy according to circumstances.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the concrete consequence indicated by the source therefore concerns the level of federal decisions. No new sanction or new military cooperation is announced. Instead, the possibility of examining these instruments is left open without the constitutional constraint envisaged by the rejected text. The distinction matters: the vote closes off a proposal, but it does not close the debate on the country's security, relations with Europe and the response to international crises.
### Three key points to keep separate
| Key point | What the source says | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Neutrality | The stricter text was rejected | Current policy remains the reference | | Bilaterals III | The Council of States opens the debate on Monday | The European dossier proceeds alongside the vote | | Bussola Initiative | Agreements with the EU would be subject to the double majority of the people and the Cantons | The relationship with Europe would have an additional political stage |
The first point concerns security and foreign policy. Deiss argues that active neutrality does not require treating aggressor and victim in the same way in every case. Hence his request to clearly condemn Israel's actions in the occupied territories and in the West Bank, without, however, indicating a specific sanction. His position is that any measures should be examined according to the circumstances.
The second and third points shift attention to European relations. The debate on Bilaterals III opens while the vote on neutrality has just been rejected. Deiss links the initiative to Pro Suisse, Azione per una Svizzera indipendente e neutrale and various figures from the UDC, arguing that its objective went beyond neutrality. The Bussola Initiative is thus presented as another step capable of shaping the country's relationship with its European neighbors.
The dossier remains institutional and related to foreign policy. For a separate in-depth look at everyday expenses, one can consult the costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. To concretely follow developments after the vote, the reader can organize their attention around four steps, all connected to the dossiers cited in the source.
### 1. Separate the result from the rejected proposal
The first step consists in distinguishing what was decided from what the initiative would have introduced. The vote rejected the stricter definition of neutrality and the restriction envisaged on the resumption of sanctions and military cooperation with alliances such as NATO. Current policy therefore remains the framework from which to start.
### 2. Follow the federal level
The second step is to observe the role of the Federal Council and Parliament. In Deiss's reading, the rejection leaves these institutions, together with citizens, the possibility of shaping foreign policy. For the reader, this means assessing future decisions without considering the vote as giving up every choice regarding international crises.
### 3. Distinguish security from the European dossier
The third step concerns the political timetable indicated by the source. On Monday, the Council of States opens the debate on Bilateral Agreements III with the European Union. It is advisable to keep this dossier separate from the vote on neutrality, but to follow them together in order to understand how security and European policy are discussed at the national level.
### 4. Check the possible role of the double majority
The fourth step is to read the Compass initiative carefully. The proposal cited by Deiss seeks to subject the adoption of agreements with the European Union to the double majority of the people and the Cantons. This is the political criterion to monitor when the issue is taken up again in the public debate.
Deiss did not indicate a specific measure against Israel: he calls for a clear condemnation of the actions in the occupied territories and in the West Bank, but believes that sanctions should be examined according to the circumstances. Swiss's first Airbus A320neo is in service with Starlink satellite technology. The company states this in a release, specifying that the first flight with the new Internet offering connected Zurich with Thessaloniki, Greece. The aircraft, named «Iseltwald», is the first in the Swiss fleet to offer the service.

The scope of permitted activities is equally clear. The connection is used to send messages, share photos and access various online services. It does not, however, include voice calls, video calls or live streams. Earphones are required for video and audio. The privacy rule adds a restriction when sharing images: other guests and the crew must be respected.

To understand when to expect the service, the equipment schedule is important. At this stage, the aircraft identified by Swiss is the A320neo Iseltwald. The next step concerns three other aircraft from the Airbus A320 family; only afterwards will the technology be gradually extended to the other aircraft. Coverage of the entire fleet is scheduled by the end of 2029. item.title: Caritas: more support for the working poor
item.description: Nearly 360'000 workers in Switzerland, 8,8% of the workforce, do not earn enough to meet family needs: Caritas proposes a minimum wage and targeted support.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Almost 360'000 workers are at risk of poverty - 8,8% of the working population cannot cover family needs - Including family members, the figure exceeds 820'000 people - Caritas proposes a minimum wage and support for families
## Key facts - Organization → Caritas - Workers concerned → almost 360'000 - Share of the working population → 8,8% - People affected including family members → over 820'000 - Measurement method → new method introduced in 2014 - Proposed measures → statutory minimum wage, predictable working hours and workloads - Supplementary benefits → already in force in five cantons - Groups most exposed → single parents and people without post-compulsory education
## Caritas's request Almost 360'000 workers in Switzerland, equivalent to 8,8% of the working population, do not earn enough to provide for their families' needs. This is Caritas's estimate, released on the eve of a new increase in health insurance premiums.
The number of people exposed to the risk of poverty, the organization emphasizes, has never been this high since the introduction of the new measurement method in 2014. If family members living in the same household are added, the total exceeds 820'000 people.
Caritas maintains that the problem of the so-called «working poor» in Switzerland is chronically underestimated. In its new position statement, it has therefore proposed «targeted measures», with the aim of strengthening support for those who work but cannot cover their family's needs.
### Proposals on work Among the proposals is a statutory minimum wage. The organization is also calling for more predictable working hours and workloads. In this area, the position statement specifies, employers also have a responsibility through collective agreements.
The package outlined by Caritas also includes supplementary benefits for families, already in force in five cantons. These should support parents whose income is insufficient to support the family.
Another proposal concerns scholarships for the labor market. These should enable the «working poor» to pursue employment-oriented continuing education, also covering lost income and any childcare costs.
According to Caritas, workers particularly at risk of poverty include, for example, single parents and people without post-compulsory education. Taking family members into account also broadens the numerical scope indicated by the organization: the problem affects the entire household. ## From wages to the family budget The Caritas snapshot concerns people who work, but whose income does not cover their family's needs. The practical analysis starts here: in-work poverty is not measured merely by looking at whether someone has a job, but at the relationship between income and the household's needs.
The reference to health insurance premiums makes the issue of costo della vita in Svizzera concrete. For residents, LAMal/KVG is mandatory; premiums are per capita and premium reductions are administered by the cantons. Insurance is neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. For a family with limited resources, the distinction matters: the premium is not the same as a deduction from one's salary, but is an expense to be included in the budget.
The scope of the proposal remains income during employment, not a change to AVS/AHV or LPP/BVG. The levers identified by Caritas are in fact the minimum wage, work schedules, family support and continuing education.
### Four levers, four effects | Proposed lever | Stated objective | |---|---| | Statutory minimum wage | Strengthen income from work | | Predictable schedules and workloads | Make work organization more stable | | Supplementary benefits for families | Support parents with insufficient income | | Scholarships for the labor market | Enable training, cover loss of income and childcare |
The table shows why the measures are not interchangeable. The minimum wage affects remuneration; predictable schedules and workloads concern the planning of family life. Supplementary benefits act on household support, while scholarships seek to remove the economic cost of training.
The fact that family benefits are already in force in five cantons introduces a concrete territorial difference. Caritas's proposal therefore asks us to look not only at the payslip, but also at the measures available in the canton and at the possibility of pursuing training without losing income or having to bear childcare costs alone.
Among the groups mentioned, single parents and people without post-compulsory education are included in the same area of risk. The position nevertheless combines distinct instruments: support for household maintenance, greater predictability of work and continuing education.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## From the problem to the practical steps Caritas' position paper proposes different instruments; for those living with insufficient income, the first practical task is not to consider them as a single benefit. It is necessary to distinguish what concerns income, what concerns the canton, what concerns working hours, and what concerns training.
### A four-step path 1. Measure available household income. The reference point is the household: Caritas speaks of the family's needs and includes in the calculation the people who live in the same household. The comparison must therefore be made between total income and maintenance needs. 2. Check the support provided by the canton. Supplementary benefits for families are already in force in five cantons. The concrete step is to check whether one's own canton is among them and how the benefits are applied to parents whose income is insufficient for their livelihood. 3. Separate training from loss of income. The labor-market scholarship proposed by Caritas should cover job-oriented continuing education, loss of income, and any childcare costs. These are the elements to compare before assessing a pathway. 4. Examine working hours, workloads, and the collective agreement. More predictable working hours and workloads are among the organization's demands. Caritas also assigns responsibility to employers through collective agreements: the worker can therefore check whether an agreement governs their employment relationship and discuss its application with the employer.
The healthcare section should be kept separate. LAMal/KVG provides per-capita premiums and reductions in cantonal premiums; the new increase mentioned by Caritas concerns health insurance premiums, not a new payroll deduction. To organize the items, one can consult the guide to busta paga svizzera and read separately the section dedicated to LAMal/cassa malati.
Not all levers have the same degree of implementation: family benefits are already in force in five cantons, whereas labor-market scholarships are presented as a proposal. The statutory minimum wage and greater predictability of working hours and workloads are also demands contained in the position paper. This distinction prevents confusing support already indicated as operational with a proposed measure.
